title: The Fire Alarm
sensory_anchor: the shriek of a fire alarm, the smell of burned toast, feet on linoleum
body: The fire alarm goes off at school. Burned toast in the cafeteria. Not a real fire. But the alarm shrieks and the students pour out and she watches them. She watches how they move. Some run. Some walk. Some freeze. Some laugh. She does none of these. She assesses. The smell is toast, not smoke. The alarm is real but the fire is not. She walks. She does not run. Running is for real fires. She walks to the exit she already mapped on the first day of school. She is outside in forty seconds. She is one of the first. Not because she is fast. Because she is ready. The ready is not a choice. It is the default. She has been ready since she was three and the line of light under the door told her whether the hallway was safe. The alarm stops. She goes back inside. Nobody noticed she was first. That is the point.

title: The Girl From Lunch
sensory_anchor: the sound of a laugh that is not performing, two people eating lunch on a curb
emotional_signature: friendship that does not require the performance
body: The girl from lunch. Seven years ago, half a sandwich. They are fourteen now. They eat lunch together every day. Not in the cafeteria. On the curb behind the gym. The curb is theirs. Nobody watches. They talk about nothing. Music. Teachers. A movie. Nothing important. The nothing is the point. The nothing is the space where she does not have to be the quiet one or the watchful one or the one who counts steps. She is just a girl on a curb eating lunch with a friend. The friend does not know about the house. The friend does not know about the stepfather. The friend knows the version of her that sits on curbs and talks about nothing. The version is real. It is not the whole version. It is a real version. She can be real here. The curb is a room without walls. The friend is a safe person. The lunch is unremarkable. The unremarkable is the measure of safety.

title: The Nice Returns
sensory_anchor: the sound of ice in a glass, a weekend afternoon, the house uncharacteristically calm
emotional_signature: kindness that is not kindness, it is the absence of the usual, and the absence is the trap
body: He is nice again. A weekend. Ice in a glass. Music from another room. The mother is relaxed. The stepfather is in a good mood. The house is almost normal. She does not trust it. She is fourteen and she has learned that the nice is a cycle. The nice comes and the nice goes and the going is worse than the not-nice that was there before the nice. She watches her mother. Her mother is smiling. Her mother believes the nice. Her mother always believes the nice. The child does not believe the nice. She waits for the nice to end. The waiting is the skill. The nice will end. She does not know when. She knows it will. She is right. By Monday, the house is the house again. The ice is gone. The music is gone. The mother is the mother again. The child is the child again. The nice was a window that closed. She does not stand in windows. She waits for them to close.

title: Running
sensory_anchor: the rhythm of feet on pavement, the sound of breathing that is not the house's breathing
emotional_signature: the body in motion is a body that is not being watched
body: She runs. Not from anything. Just runs. The track team. She did not try out. The coach saw her running during PE and told her to try out. She tried out. She made it. Running is not about speed. Running is about leaving. Every lap is a departure. Every lap is also a return, but the return is a choice, not a trap. She runs and the house gets smaller behind her and the air is hers and the pavement is steady and her feet hit it in a rhythm that is not the rhythm of the house. The rhythm is hers. She controls the pace. She controls the distance. She controls the return. Running is the first thing she controls. She will run for the rest of her life. Not on a team. Just running. Running is the civilian version of the exit strategy.

title: The Art Teacher
sensory_anchor: charcoal dust, the smell of fixative, a teacher's hand on her shoulder for a moment
emotional_signature: being seen for what she makes, not for what she performs
body: The art teacher looks at her drawing. The drawing is not good. It is real. The teacher sees something in it. The teacher says: you see differently. The child does not understand. The teacher says: most people draw what they think things look like. You draw what you see. The child shrugs. The teacher puts the drawing on the wall. The child does not want it on the wall. The wall is visibility. Visibility is danger. But the teacher put it there and the teacher is an authority and she does not challenge authorities she does not need to challenge. She looks at the drawing on the wall. It is hers. It is on the wall. It is visible. She is visible. She survives the visibility. Nothing bad happens. This is a new data point. Visibility is sometimes safe. She files this. The file is small. It will grow.

title: The Party
sensory_anchor: loud music, the smell of cheap cologne and spilled soda, the geometry of a crowded room
emotional_signature: reading a room full of people who are not reading her
body: A party. She does not want to go. She goes. The friend from the curb wants to go. The party is loud. The music is too loud. She maps the room in three seconds: exits, rooms, the kitchen, the back door. She stays near the back door. The friend is on the dance floor. She watches. She reads the room. Who is drinking. Who is watching who. Who is about to do something stupid. She does not know she is doing this. She thinks she is just standing there. She is standing there and running an assessment. The friend comes back. The friend is happy. The friend does not notice the assessment. Good. The assessment is invisible. She wants it to be invisible. She wants to be the person who is at the party, not the person who is watching the party. She is both. She is fifteen and she is already both and she does not know if both is normal. She suspects it is not.

title: The Night She Left the House
sensory_anchor: the front door at midnight, the cold air outside, the street empty
emotional_signature: leaving before the thing happens is better than leaving after
body: She leaves the house. Not permanently. She walks out the front door at midnight because the stepfather is in a mood and the mood is escalating and she knows the escalation pattern and she does not want to be in the house when it peaks. She walks. The street is empty. The air is cold. She walks to the end of the block and back. The house is quiet when she returns. The peak passed. She goes to her room. She is not running away. She is running the clock. The mood has a duration. The duration is predictable. She waits it out somewhere else. She does not know this is a tactical withdrawal. She is fifteen. She calls it going for a walk. The walk is a skill. The walk is how you survive a thing without being in the room where the thing happens. She will use this skill again. In different houses. In different countries. For different reasons. The walk is always the same. Leave. Wait. Return.

title: The School Counselor
sensory_anchor: a small office, the smell of coffee and paper, a question that is too specific
emotional_signature: the system is not the solution, the system is the risk
body: The school counselor calls her in. The counselor asks questions. How is home. How is the family. How are things. The questions are too specific. The counselor has heard something. Maybe the neighbor. Maybe a teacher. The child lies. The lies are smooth. The lies are the performance. The performance is perfect. The counselor writes something down. The child sees the writing. The counselor says: you can talk to me. The child knows she cannot. The counselor is the system. The system can intervene. Intervention makes it worse. The stepfather will know. The stepfather will adjust. The adjustment will be worse than the current state. She smiles. She says everything is fine. She leaves. The counselor does not call her back. The counselor believed the performance. The performance worked. The performance is not a lie. The performance is a wall. The wall is load-bearing.

title: The Journal
sensory_anchor: a notebook with a lock, the sound of the click, the pen on paper that is only hers
emotional_signature: the one place where the performance stops
body: She keeps a journal. A notebook with a lock. The lock is cheap and would not stop anyone who really wanted in. The lock is a symbol. The symbol says: this is mine. She writes in it at night. She writes about the house. She writes about the stepfather. She writes about the grandmother. She writes about the rage. The rage on paper is different from the rage in her chest. The rage on paper has been spent. The rage in her chest is banked. She writes until the rage on the page is enough for tonight. Then she locks the book. She hides it. She sleeps. The journal is the first safe room she builds herself. Not the grandmother's kitchen. Not the summer grass. A room made of paper and a cheap lock. The room is hers. She built it. She decides what goes in it. She decides who reads it. Nobody reads it. The room stays safe.

title: The Gymnasium Floor
sensory_anchor: polished wood, the squeak of sneakers, the echo of a ball bouncing in an empty space
emotional_signature: the body in a space that is not the house
body: The gymnasium after practice. The others have left. She stays. She shoots baskets. She is not good at basketball. She is good at being alone in a large space. The gymnasium is not the house. The gymnasium is open and bright and nobody is monitoring the doors. She shoots. She misses. She shoots. She misses. She shoots. The ball goes in. The sound of the ball through the net is a sound that is not the sound of the house. The echo of the gymnasium is not the echo of the hallways. She stays until the lights go off. The darkness in the gymnasium is different from the darkness in the house. The darkness in the gymnasium is just darkness. The darkness in the house is information. She stays in the gymnasium darkness. It is just dark. She breathes. The darkness does not care about her. That is the best thing about it.
